excerpt: Paid ads and organic results play by different rules. Here is how rankings differ between PPC and SEO, and what that means for your marketing budget.

faqs.a: No. You cannot buy organic rankings. Paid placements are clearly labelled and sit above the organic list. To move up organically you need strong content, a healthy website, and quality links pointing to it.
faqs.q: Can I pay Google to rank my website higher organically?

faqs.a: They stack very well together. PPC tells you which keywords convert, and SEO builds long term traffic on those same keywords. Many businesses run both so they are not fully dependent on either channel.
faqs.q: Should I run PPC and SEO at the same time?

faqs.a: It is not free in effort. SEO needs content, technical fixes, and ongoing work, which costs time or money. The difference is that organic clicks keep coming after the work is done, while PPC clicks stop the day you stop paying.

intro:
Search for almost anything on Google and you will see two kinds of results on the page. The top few have a small "Sponsored" label, and everything below them is the organic list. The sponsored ones come from PPC, which means pay per click. The organic ones come from SEO, which means search engine optimization.

Both are ways of getting your business in front of people who are searching. But the way you earn your place is completely different, and so is what your position costs you over time. Business owners often mix them up, so here is the difference in plain terms.
keyword: how is ranking different when comparing ppc vs seo
meta: PPC and SEO both put you on Google, but rankings work very differently in each. A plain-English guide for business owners.

body: PPC rankings work like an auction. You pick a keyword, set a bid, and Google places your ad based on your bid and how relevant your ad and landing page are. If you raise your bid, you can jump to the top of the page within hours. There is no mystery about it: money plus a decent ad buys the position.

SEO rankings work like a reputation. Google looks at your content, your website's technical health, how fast it loads, and how many trustworthy sites link to you. Nobody pays Google for an organic position, and you cannot negotiate one. You earn it over time, and you keep it only as long as you deserve it.
sections.heading: You buy one ranking and earn the other

body: This is the biggest practical difference for a business owner. When you pause a PPC campaign, your ads disappear from the results immediately. Every click you ever got had a price tag, and the traffic stops the second the budget runs out.

SEO behaves the opposite way. The work is slow at the start: writing helpful content, fixing technical issues, and building links can take months before anything moves. But once a page ranks, it keeps bringing visitors without a per-click cost. It is not free, because you paid in work or agency fees, but the traffic keeps arriving long after the work is done.
sections.heading: Paid traffic stops the moment you stop paying

body: PPC is built for the short term. Launching a new product, running a seasonal sale, or testing whether people actually want what you sell: all of these are jobs PPC does well. You can be in front of buyers today, and you can measure exactly what each click cost you.

SEO is built for the long term. It is how you become the business people find every time they search for what you do, without paying for each visit. Most smart businesses use PPC to get going and learn what works, then invest in SEO to own that traffic permanently. The two channels feed each other nicely.
sections.heading: One is a sprint, the other is a marathon

body: With PPC you always know your position is temporary. A competitor can outbid you tomorrow, and your costs rise whenever demand for that keyword rises. Your ranking is only as safe as your budget.

With SEO your position is earned but not guaranteed. Google updates its system regularly, and a competitor can overtake you with better content or a stronger site. The difference is that an SEO ranking usually decays slowly, giving you time to respond, while a PPC position can vanish overnight if you cut the budget.
sections.heading: How stable each ranking is

body: PPC gives you near perfect measurement. Every click has a cost, every conversion can be tracked, and you can see your return on investment for every keyword by the end of the day.

SEO measurement is fuzzier but broader. You can see traffic growth, ranking positions, and conversions, but tying every dollar of revenue back to a specific SEO task is harder. What SEO gives you instead is leverage: the same article can bring you customers for years without another dollar spent on clicks.
sections.heading: Measuring what you get for your money

body: Ask yourself two questions. First, how fast do you need results? If you need customers this week, PPC is the honest answer. Second, how long will you be in business? If the answer is years, SEO is almost always worth the investment, because owned traffic gets cheaper over time.

Most businesses do best with both. PPC buys you speed and data. SEO buys you lasting visibility. Understanding that they rank you in completely different ways is the first step to spending your budget wisely.
sections.heading: So which one should your business use?

title: PPC vs SEO: How Rankings Really Differ
